vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: make-design-md
Version: 1.0.0

The 'make-design-md' skill is designed to analyze website design styles from URLs, HTML files, or screenshots and generate a structured DESIGN.md document following the Google design.md specification. It uses standard agent capabilities like WebFetch and Read to process inputs and provides instructions for using the legitimate '@google/design.md' CLI tool for validation. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and runtime instructions align with its stated purpose (extracting design tokens from a URL/HTML/screenshot and producing a DESIGN.md); it is instruction-only, requests no credentials, and does not contain unexplained install steps or hidden endpoints.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (generate DESIGN.md from a website/HTML/screenshot) matches the instructions in SKILL.md. Required capabilities (fetching a URL, reading a provided HTML file or screenshot, extracting CSS/visual tokens, producing markdown/html previews, and optionally running the Google design.md CLI) are coherent with the skill's purpose. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md stays focused on the stated task: fetch provided URLs, read user-supplied files, extract tokens, and produce DESIGN.md and preview HTML. Two operational notes: (1) the skill presumes the agent has WebFetch/Read tools — these will access the URL or file the user gives, so the agent could fetch internal endpoints or read local files if the user supplies them (expected for this feature, but a potential SSRF/local-file-read vector if misused). (2) SKILL.md suggests using 'npx @google/design.md' for lint/export — that would invoke npm/network activity when run.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no code files (instruction-only), which minimizes on-disk risk. However, SKILL.md recommends running npx commands for validation/export; invoking npx will fetch packages from npm and execute them locally — a normal but nontrivial runtime action that users/operators should be aware of.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. The instructions do not ask for secrets or unrelated environment data. This is proportionate to its stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent or elevated platform privileges. It is user-invocable and relies on the agent's existing WebFetch/Read capabilities — normal for this skill's function.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent with its goal of extracting design tokens and generating DESIGN.md. Before using it: (1) only supply URLs and local file paths you trust — the agent will fetch/read whatever you give it (avoid internal-only URLs or sensitive local files to reduce SSRF/local-file exposure). (2) Running 'npx @google/design.md' will download and execute code from npm—review that package or run in a sandbox if you are cautious. (3) Confirm the agent's WebFetch/Read tools run in an environment you control (so fetched data or local files aren't uploaded to external services you don't expect). If you want higher assurance, ask for the exact commands the agent will run (or run the npx commands yourself) rather than allowing automatic execution.
